title: A Atlas for the Uniform
premise: In the waning months of the Republic of Vessany, Noor Lockridge carries diplomatic codes between ministries, a job that demands invisibility. When a census taker's probing question exposes the forged identity of his found family—the retired archivist Mirela and her ward, Tavi—Noor is conscripted by a desperate foreign attaché to smuggle a ledger proving the government's coming purge past three checkpoints before the year ends. Each checkpoint costs him something: a name, a memory, a person he loves. At the final gate on New Year's Eve, Noor must choose between the ledger and Tavi, and discovers the codes he has carried all along were the map out for all of them.
about_author: Q. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of collapsed states. They write about the people history forgets to count, and live between two languages and one border.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. During a routine census visit, a question about household lineage threatens to expose Mirela's forged papers, and Noor's practiced silences fail him for the first time. The census taker, Halvard, notes something down and leaves. Emotional beat: the fragile safety of seven years cracks open in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Mirela burns what she can and reveals to Noor that she once worked in the Ministry of Records, and that the census marks households for 'review.' She gives Noor a hidden key to her old office. Emotional beat: the mentor becomes vulnerable; the found family's history deepens and darkens.

chapters.title: The Attaché's Offer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The foreign attaché Serevan intercepts Noor at the ministry, showing him a ledger that documents the purge schedule, and offers escape papers for his whole household if Noor carries it past three checkpoints by New Year's Eve. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as choice; Noor accepts because refusing means Tavi's name on a list.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Bridge of Names
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the river checkpoint, guards cross-reference names against the census rolls, and Noor must give up his own documented identity, surrendering the name he has used since childhood, to pass. Emotional beat: the cost made flesh—identity as the first thing the state takes.

chapters.title: Tavi Follows
chapters.summary: Tavi's POV. Fifteen-year-old Tavi, sensing the household unraveling, stows away after Noor and trails him to the second checkpoint city, forcing Noor to abandon his careful route. Emotional beat: love as complication; the ward insists on being family, not cargo.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Noor and Tavi's alternating POV. The Ministry of Records is set aflame to destroy evidence, and Mirela is inside retrieving the key's counterpart. They pull her out, but the ledger's authentication page burns in the rescue. Emotional beat: found family forged in fire; grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: What Halvard Knew
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The census taker, revealed as a reluctant informant, recognizes Noor at a tea house and, instead of reporting him, explains the purge's mechanics and warns him the third checkpoint has his description. Emotional beat: an enemy's unexpected mercy complicates every certainty Noor holds.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Century's Turn
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the border gate on New Year's Eve, guards detain Tavi as leverage, demanding the ledger in exchange for the boy. Noor realizes the codes he has memorized for seven years contain the gate's release sequence. Emotional beat: the climax—everything he has learned about silence becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: The Courier's Choice
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor recites the codes, opening the gate for a crowd of listed households, and walks through carrying Tavi's hand and the ledger both, while Serevan's men close in behind. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into defiance; the courier finally delivers himself.

chapters.title: An Atlas for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV, epilogue. In exile, the three of them begin mapping the routes of escapees into a hand-drawn atlas, and the ledger reaches the foreign press. Noor, nameless by choice, signs the first copy. Emotional beat: memory rebuilt as a gift; identity remade as a map for others to follow.
